exposure: previous experience with severity of RSV
parental vaccination status during childhood and current pregnancy
outcome: preference between maternal vaccination and neonatal immunization
cohort: 1001 pregnant women (mean age 31.1 years) and their partners (mean age 33.2 years) in the Netherlands, who were on average 24 weeks pregnant at the time of the survey.
finding: The overall acceptability for both RSV prevention strategies was high (87%), with a majority (75.3% of pregnant women, 71.6% of partners) favoring maternal vaccination over passive infant immunization, particularly among those with existing children and an intention to breastfeed.
cross-section timing: During pregnancy, at an average of 24 weeks gestational age.
gest_age: Mothers averaged 24 weeks gestational age at the time of the survey.
